turn_prompts: Start a new fenced authoring conversation, read validation_environment_contract and validation_repair_context first, then read the prior candidate snapshot, validation_receipt, verification_contract, and any critic findings. Critic findings are optional; validation_repair_context is the primary diagnosis. In the authoring workspace, source/ is read-only and task/ is the only writable candidate directory; write only the fixed candidate files under task/. Each repair turn has exactly one candidate-validation opportunity: call harbor_validate_candidate at most once in this turn. A rejected receipt ends this turn; do not call the tool again until the next prompt. When provisioning Debian packages in environment/Dockerfile, switch the default Debian APT sources from HTTP to HTTPS before apt-get update; the controlled build network permits HTTPS egress only. When the frozen VerificationContract invokes test.sh through sh, both test.sh and solution/solve.sh must be POSIX sh compatible: do not use set -o pipefail, bash arrays, [[, or other Bash-only syntax.

Read validation_repair_context before critic findings; critic findings are optional context only. Correct the documented failing layer in the candidate workspace, preserving validation_environment_contract: validator /source and /task are read-only, /work is the writable copy where solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh operate. Call harbor_validate_candidate once to create the next immutable snapshot and receipt.

If validation remains rejected, compare validation_repair_context, repair_guidance, the current candidate, the frozen VerificationContract, baseline behavior, and Oracle behavior. Apply one focused correction and call harbor_validate_candidate once; do not alter frozen source inputs, source/, /source, or the verifier contract.

Use validation_repair_context to repair the narrow failing layer: layout, environment provisioning, baseline, Oracle, coverage, or integrity. Runtime validation is no-network with a read-only root filesystem, so keep runtime writes under /work or /tmp/harbor-* and keep scripts POSIX sh when the contract invokes them through sh, then validate the replacement candidate once.

Only change environment/Dockerfile when validation_repair_context identifies an environment-layer failure; if environment provisioning already passed host_candidate_verify or an earlier repair receipt, keep environment/Dockerfile unchanged and repair only the failing code/test layer. When provisioning is genuinely required for Rust/Cargo browser-wasm failures, provision generic wasm/browser tools in environment/Dockerfile during Docker build; runtime dependencies must come from the pinned base image, repository vendor tree, or another frozen input. Set CARGO_HOME=/work/.cargo-home and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/work/.cargo-target, and do not copy full Cargo registry or target caches into limited /tmp.

Re-read validation_repair_context and the most recent receipt before changing files. Preserve every successful constraint while correcting only the remaining failure, and call harbor_validate_candidate once after the repair.

Continue the bounded repair loop from the latest immutable candidate and validation_repair_context. Do not hide failures, bypass the verifier, or substitute a different repository, command, or source revision; validate the next focused correction once.

Use the final available repair turn only for a correction supported by validation_repair_context, repair_guidance, and the latest receipt. Check that instruction, task metadata, environment, solution, test script, and tests analysis agree with the frozen task and verification contracts, then call harbor_validate_candidate once and rely on its immutable receipt; a passing receipt ends the repair loop.
